hero.headline: Not every local race lists party affiliation on the ballot.
hero.body: Selected 2026 races across Gage County, including declared write-in candidates, with documented political affiliations and cited sources. Some voters consider political affiliation alongside a candidate’s experience, qualifications, statements, and priorities when evaluating people who may make decisions about public budgets, services, or tax levies. The races on your ballot depend on where you live.

guide.heading: How to read this directory
guide.introduction: Published by the Gage County GOP. The directory covers selected races, not every contest on your ballot.
guide.noticeBody: Candidates receive the same sourcing and presentation standards. Inclusion in this directory does not indicate a Gage County GOP endorsement.
guide.verificationIntroduction: Different sources establish different facts. Candidate cards identify the source used for each displayed claim.
guide.correctionIntroduction: Source links and review dates appear on each candidate card.
guide.correctionPrompt: If an entry appears inaccurate or outdated, send a supporting public source to:

context.heading: What “nonpartisan” means here
paragraphs: A nonpartisan race is one in which party labels do not appear beside candidate names on the ballot. A candidate may still have a publicly documented political affiliation.
Registered affiliation, ballot party, and participation in a party primary are different facts. Each affiliation label identifies which evidence supports it.
County, state, and federal sections also include partisan races. Consult official election materials for the contests on your ballot.

items.question: Are all races in this directory nonpartisan?
items.answer: No. In a nonpartisan race, party labels do not appear beside candidate names on the ballot. This directory also includes partisan county, state, and federal races.

items.question: Does a listed affiliation mean the candidate is officially running as a party nominee?
items.answer: Not necessarily. The directory includes races with different ballot rules. A publicly documented political affiliation should not be treated as proof of nomination status; consult official election materials for the specific race.

items.question: How was this information verified?
items.answer: Registered affiliation, ballot party, primary participation, and election results are supported by different sources.

items.question: Why are some candidates listed under primary history?
items.answer: These candidates participated in the primary and are not currently listed for the general election. The card identifies non-advancement, withdrawal, or absence from the final list when supported by a source.

items.question: What happens if an affiliation changes?
items.answer: The entry should be updated when a reliable public source documents the change. Each card shows when its source was reviewed.

items.question: Does this site endorse candidates?
items.answer: Inclusion in this directory does not indicate a Gage County GOP endorsement. Candidates receive the same sourcing and presentation standards.

items.question: How can an error be corrected?
items.answer: Send a supporting public source to the correction contact shown in this guide.
